content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Kubernetes Architecture and Control Plane Components"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Kubernetes control plane is the brain of the cluster, responsible for maintaining the desired state of your applications, making global decisions, and detecting and responding to cluster events. This tutorial dives deep into the core components that make up the Kubernetes control plane."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of the Control Plane"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A standard Kubernetes control plane consists of several distinct services and processes running either as containers or systemd services. These components work in unison to orchestrate containerized workloads across the worker nodes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Kube-apiserver: The frontend for the Kubernetes control plane, exposing the Kubernetes API REST endpoints."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Etcd: A consistent and highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes backing store for all cluster data."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Kube-scheduler: Watches for newly created pods with no assigned node, and selects a node for them to run on."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Kube-controller-manager: Runs controller processes that regulate the state of the cluster through the API server."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Inspecting Control Plane Pods"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a clustered environment (such as one bootstrapped via kubeadm), the control plane components run as static pods inside the \"kube-system\" namespace. You can inspect these pods using the kubectl CLI tool."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l tier=control-plane"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Detailed Breakdown of the API Server and Etcd"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The \"kube-apiserver\" is designed to scale horizontally. It processes REST operations, validates data, and configures objects for pods, services, and replication controllers. Meanwhile, \"etcd\" stores the absolute source of truth for the cluster. Because of its critical role, etcd requires proper backup strategies and low-latency disk storage."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key endpoint health"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding the interplay between the API server, etcd, scheduler, and controller manager is essential for troubleshooting cluster issues, optimizing performance, and designing secure, highly-available Kubernetes architectures."}]
